newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: EMU critieria secondary to growth - Austria official.
newsitem.headline: EMU critieria secondary to growth - Austria official.

text.p: A top Austrian finance ministry official said in an interview on Wednesday that employment and growth were more important than a strict interpretation of the convergence criteria for Europe's planned single currency.

Wolfgang Ruttenstorfer, secretary of state in the finance ministry, told daily Wirtschaftsblatt: "One has to keep an eye on employment and economic development. That has to take precedence to strict adherence to the three percent (deficit) limit as early as in 1997."

The Maastricht treaty on European monetary union (EMU) stipulates a range of economic targets for countries wanting to join EMU, including limiting budget deficits to three percent of gross domestic product and public debt to 60 percent.
Ruttenstorfer, who is in charge of Austria's preparations for EMU, said the speed with which countries attempted to meet these criteria should be reduced.
"With a view to the weak economy, a moderate consolidation is more sensible," he said. "It's about the speed with which the convergence criteria have to be met. That should be reduced."
Austria is convinced it will be among the first group of nations to join EMU and experts agree that its deficit is set to meet the three percent threshold this year.

According to a recent poll, every second Austrian is against the single currency. Austria's powerful labour unions are not strictly against the project but have pressed the government to place greater weight on employment issues in the run-up to EMU.
